title: Use AI to Code
subtitle: From idea to something that runs — with AI
description: The flagship Teachy path. Learn the real skill of 2026: describe what you want, get AI to build it, run it, and fix it when it’s wrong — on your Mac, with a 1:1 tutor beside you. No CS degree required.
learningOutcomes: Open an AI that can help you write code
Describe a tiny project in plain language
Get a first working version from the AI
Run or open the result so you can see it
Ask for a change and verify it landed
Save the project somewhere you’ll find again
Say in one sentence what you built

goals.title: Open your AI
goals.goal: Have an AI coding helper open — Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or similar — so you can start building.
goals.coachAsk: Help me open an AI that can write code with me — Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor is fine. Point at how I get started.
goals.doneWhen: An AI chat or AI coding tool is open and recognizable on screen (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot, or similar).
tips: Browser Claude or ChatGPT is perfect for beginners
Cursor is great if you already have it
Signing in is OK if the tool asks

goals.title: Ask for something tiny
goals.goal: Send a clear first prompt for a tiny project — like a one-page site, a calculator, or a to-do list — in plain language.
goals.coachAsk: I want to build something tiny with AI. Help me write a clear first prompt — not too big — and point at where I should send it.
goals.doneWhen: A clear project prompt is visible in the AI chat input or as a sent message (a small app, page, or script request).
tips: Small is better: one page, one feature
Say what it should look like and what it should do
Example vibe: “Make a single HTML page with a tip calculator”

goals.title: Get a first version
goals.goal: Receive a first version of the project from the AI — code, files, or a scaffold you can use.
goals.coachAsk: The AI should give me a first version now. Point at the reply or code I should use, and tell me what to do next in one short beat.
goals.doneWhen: AI-generated code, files, or a clear project scaffold is visible in the conversation or editor.
tips: If it asks clarifying questions, answer simply
You don’t need to understand every line yet

goals.title: See it run
goals.goal: Open or run the result so something real is on screen — a browser preview, a window, or output that proves it works.
goals.coachAsk: How do I actually see this thing run? Help me open a preview, save a file and open it, or run it — point at the next move.
goals.doneWhen: A running or previewed result is visible — browser page, app window, terminal output, or live preview of the project.
tips: HTML often means save as .html and open in a browser
If the AI gave a link or preview, use that
“It runs” beats “it looks smart in the chat”

goals.title: Change something
goals.goal: Ask the AI to change the project — color, text, feature, or fix — and get an updated version.
goals.coachAsk: I want to change something about what we built. Help me ask the AI clearly, then point at where the update shows up.
goals.doneWhen: An updated AI response or edited project is visible that reflects a requested change.
tips: Point at what you dislike: “make the button bigger” beats “make it better”

goals.title: Verify the change
goals.goal: Confirm the change in the running project — refresh preview, re-open the file, or check the UI so you know it landed.
goals.coachAsk: How do I check that the change actually landed in the running thing? Point at what I should look at.
goals.doneWhen: The running or previewed project shows the requested change (or the learner has clearly checked the updated output).
tips: Refresh the browser if it’s a web page
This is the habit that separates builders from copy-pasters

goals.title: Save it for later
goals.goal: Save the project somewhere durable on your Mac — a folder, file, or project you’ll find again.
goals.coachAsk: Help me save this project somewhere obvious on my Mac so I don’t lose it. Point at how I should save or where to put the files.
goals.doneWhen: The project is saved as a file, folder, or named project on disk (Finder, editor save dialog, or clearly saved project UI).
tips: Desktop or a Documents/Projects folder is fine
Name it something you’ll recognize next week

goals.title: Name what you built
goals.goal: Write or say one clear sentence: what you built and that you used AI to do it.
goals.coachAsk: Last step — help me write one sentence that says what I built with AI. Point at a notes app, the chat, or anywhere I can type it.
goals.doneWhen: A short written sentence is visible describing what was built (notes, chat, doc, or similar).
tips: Example: “I built a tip calculator webpage with AI.”
This is your proof — keep it
